The first three objects together didn't light the machine. If a single nexiom is enough to light it, the nexioms must be among semoval, saneki and mubades. Testing one of those alone should show whether it is a nexiom under that rule. It may also show whether the machine needs both nexioms together.

TEST: semoval
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Under the simplest rule, where any single nexiom lights the machine, the first two tests leave only saneki and mubades as nexioms. Under the rule where both nexioms must be present together, those two tests tell me little. Testing saneki and mubades together covers both cases. If the machine lights, the answer is saneki and mubades under either rule. If it stays dark, I'll know neither of those simple rules fits this pair, and I'll use the last test to sort it out.

TEST: saneki, mubades
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

No simple rule fits all three results:
- **Any single nexiom lights the machine:** this is ruled out. The nexioms would have to be saneki and mubades, but that pair stayed dark.
- **Both nexioms must be present together:** 11 pairs remain possible. These are any one of zebile, dopaban or daforor paired with any one of semoval, saneki or mubades. Semoval–saneki and semoval–mubades are also still possible.
- **Exactly one nexiom must be present:** 4 pairs remain possible. These are zebile–dopaban, zebile–daforor, dopaban–daforor and saneki–mubades.

One test can't separate all of these candidates, so I can't guarantee the right answer. I'll test a mixed group that splits the candidates under both remaining rules. Then I'll give my best guess.

TEST: zebile, semoval, saneki
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

No single rule is certain, but the four dark results narrow things down.

- **Any single nexiom lights the machine:** ruled out by test 3.
- **Both nexioms must be present together:** this rule still fits, with 8 possible pairs left. These are zebile–mubades, dopaban–semoval, dopaban–saneki, dopaban–mubades, daforor–semoval, daforor–saneki, daforor–mubades and semoval–mubades.
- **Exactly one nexiom must be present:** only one pair fits. Semoval alone stayed dark, so semoval is not a nexiom. Test 4 rules out any pair with exactly one of zebile or saneki. That eliminates zebile–dopaban, zebile–daforor and saneki–mubades. Dopaban–daforor fits every result, because test 1 contained both nexioms and the other tests contained none.

Dopaban–daforor is the only answer that one rule pins down exactly, so it is my best guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = dopaban, daforor
One last question. If only daforor were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

It depends on which rule the machine follows, and my tests didn't settle that.

- **Exactly one nexiom must be present:** this is the rule behind my answer of dopaban and daforor. Under it, daforor alone has exactly one nexiom, so the machine **would light up**. This is also the only rule that pointed to a single pair.
- **Both nexioms must be present together:** this rule also fits all four results. Under it, daforor alone could never light the machine, since one object can't supply both nexioms.

I'll stay consistent with my answer and say yes, but this is a guess resting on that rule.
